topic: energy-efficient computing; embedded systems; distributed data; deep learning; federated learning
status: four fixed-frame uniform-random full texts across four arXiv submission periods; bounded, falsifiable reporting/reproducibility hypothesis; not a prevalence estimate or novelty claim
claim: The four sampled papers use materially different energy constructs: a model-based estimate driven by system counters; a formal safe worst-case dynamic-energy target; assumed component wattage multiplied by runtime; and a table of whole-experiment Wh whose acquisition procedure is not reproducible from the paper. These are not directly rankable as one energy-efficiency outcome. The evidence supports testing a typed energy-accounting contract that declares estimand, system boundary, meter/model/counter and calibration, workload and achieved service quality, time window, assumptions/exclusions, uncertainty, and repetitions. The sample also contains counterevidence to any blanket claim that energy reporting is absent: two papers disclose their model inputs/assumptions and the theory paper clearly distinguishes worst-case from typical energy. The actionable gap is heterogeneous or incomplete provenance, not a claim that any reported number is false.

sources.title: Data Placement and Replica Selection for Improving Co-location in Distributed Environments

§1: MySQL TPC-H runtime increases with parallelism, potentially due to nested-loop join implementation; custom processor runtime stays roughly constant while modeled energy rises

sources.title: On the Limitations of Analysing Worst-Case Dynamic Energy of Processing
locators: Abstract and §§5–8: exact operand-dependent worst-case switching is NP-hard; useful safe tight approximation ruled out in model
§2: random-operand average instruction costs cannot be treated as safe upper bounds
§7: dynamic core-energy contribution can be a smaller fraction of system energy when caches, memory, peripherals, and other components dominate

locators: §III-C: η=F1/E; §IV-A: simulated FL setup and one NVIDIA RTX 6000 Ada listed
Table I: 10 clients, 30 rounds, five local epochs, deterministic balanced i.i.d. partition
Table II: whole-experiment Wh/runtime/quality values; method does not specify energy meter/counter, calculation, system boundary, idle handling, or repeat variance

counterevidence: The 2013 system paper names its Mantis-derived server power model and the dstat counters supplied to it; its modeled estimate has methodological provenance even though it is not direct metering.

The 2024 DDLP paper states its assumed power values, 20-seed aggregation, and an important omitted storage-transfer interval, allowing readers to identify a key boundary rather than treating its estimate as an unexplained meter reading.

The 2016 paper's worst-case target is explicitly theoretical and must not be treated as evidence that operational mean energy is inherently unmeasurable; the 2026 paper's unspecified Wh procedure is a reporting gap, not proof of incorrect values.
falsifiable_test: Sample energy-related systems papers across topic and year strata; independently code the declared estimand (mean/task, marginal, whole-system, or safe worst case), system boundary, acquisition method/calibration, workload and achieved quality/deadline, exclusions/time window, uncertainty, and repeats. For a subset with runnable artifacts or accessible hardware, have independent teams reproduce energy and rank systems using both original reporting and a typed accounting contract. Measure field completeness, reproduction success, between-team variance, and rank changes when reasonable boundaries/meters change. The hypothesis is weakened if the typed contract does not improve reproducibility or reduce unsupported cross-paper rankings, or if rankings remain robust despite accounting-field differences.
